topic: Ionization of Weak Acids and Bases
title: Weak Acids, Ka and pKa Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Vinegar goes on a salad but hydrochloric acid burns skin, and both bottles say 0.1 M. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 6, Equilibrium) Aarav reads two bottles in the college lab: 0.1 M acetic acid has pH 2.9, while 0.1 M hydrochloric acid has pH 1.

On the molecule bench you will watch 100 acetic acid molecules where only 1 or 2 break up, and meet the degree of ionization (about 1.3 % at 0.1 M). We build the acid ionization constant Ka and pKa with NCERT values (HF 3.5 x 10^-4, acetic acid 1.74 x 10^-5, HCN 4.9 x 10^-10), derive Ka = c alpha^2 / (1 - alpha) and alpha = square root of Ka/c step by step, cover weak bases and Kb (ammonia 1.77 x 10^-5), Ka x Kb = Kw and pKa + pKb = 14, and why Ka1 > Ka2 for acids with more than one proton. Then the pH of 0.1 M acetic acid (2.88), the dilution trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 67 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

2:27 Weak bases, Kb and Ka x Kb = Kw
